source_refs.note: Book p. 4-5: 1.3 introduction, (i) Algebraic Functions (definition, examples), (ii) Transcendental Functions (definition, examples)

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Aaj se hum Class XII Mathematics ke us hisse mein dakhil ho rahe hain jahan functions ki ek nayi dunya khulti hai. Ab tak aap ne zyada tar aise functions dekhe hain jo seedhi saadi algebra se bante hain. Is section mein hum functions ko do bari families mein baantenge: algebraic functions aur transcendental functions. Yeh do classes mathematics mein buniyadi (basic) hain aur asal zindagi ke bohat se masail, jaise aabadi ka barhna ya dawa ka jism mein kam hona, inhi se model kiye jate hain. Is section ka asal focus fundamental transcendental functions par hai, yani exponential aur logarithmic functions par.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Zara yaad kijiye Class XI mein aap ne kaun se functions use kiye: polynomials jaise \(x^{2} - 5x + 6\), rational functions jaise \(\frac{1}{x-2}\), aur roots jaise \(\sqrt{x}\). In sab ko banane ke liye sirf jama, tafreeq, zarb, taqseem aur roots kaafi thay. Lekin \(e^{x}\), \(\ln x\) aur \(\sin x\) jaise functions in operations se kabhi nahin bante; yeh algebra ki had se "aage" nikal jate hain. Transcendental lafz ka matlab hi yahi hai: had se aage jane wala. Yeh farq is liye zaroori hai ke poora Unit 1 aage inhi transcendental functions (exponential, logarithmic, hyperbolic) ke graphs aur properties par chalega.

Kitab ki definition: ek function \(y = f(x)\) algebraic kehlata hai agar woh is qisam ki ek polynomial equation ko satisfy kare (yani us equation mein rakhne se dono taraf barabar ho jayein):
\[P_{n}(x)y^{n} + P_{n-1}(x)y^{n-1} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + P_{1}(x)y + P_{0}(x) = 0\]
jahan har \(P_{i}(x)\) \(x\) ka ek polynomial hai, \(i = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, n\) ke liye, aur \(i = 1, 2, 3, \ldots, n\) mein se kam az kam (at least) ek \(P_{i}(x)\) identically zero nahin hai (yani har \(x\) par zero nahin hota).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "atleast" ek hi lafz likhti hai; sahi spelling do alag lafz "at least" hai. Definition ki mathematics mein koi farq nahin parta, sirf spelling ki ghalti hai.

Ghabraiye mat, is lambi equation ka seedha matlab yeh hai: ek function algebraic hai agar woh \(x\) se sirf mehdood (finite) tadaad mein algebraic operations laga kar banaya ja sake, yani addition (jama), subtraction (tafreeq), multiplication (zarb), division (taqseem) aur \(n^{\text{th}}\) roots. Jaise ek bawarchi sirf chaar paanch bartan use kar ke khana banaye: agar khana sirf in bartanon se ban gaya to woh "algebraic" hai.
Kitab ki misalein: \(f(x) = 2x^{2} - 3x\), \(g(x) = \frac{x^{2}+1}{x-3},\ x \ne 3\), \(h(x) = (x+1)^{3/2}\) aur \(k(x) = \sqrt{x+1}\), yeh sab algebraic functions hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ab dekhte hain ke yeh chaaron function waqai polynomial equation ko kaise satisfy karte hain. Tareeqa simple hai: function ko \(y\) likhiye, phir roots aur fractions ko hata dijiye.
\(f\): \(y - (2x^{2} - 3x) = 0\). Yahan \(n = 1\), \(P_{1}(x) = 1\) aur \(P_{0}(x) = -(2x^{2} - 3x)\).
\(g\): dono taraf \(x - 3\) se zarb dein: \((x - 3)y - (x^{2} + 1) = 0\). Fraction khatam!
\(h\): \(y = (x+1)^{3/2}\) ka dono taraf square lein: \(y^{2} - (x + 1)^{3} = 0\).
\(k\): \(y = \sqrt{x+1}\) ka square lein: \(y^{2} - (x + 1) = 0\).
Har jagah humein \(y\) ki ek polynomial equation mil gayi jis ke coefficients \(x\) ke polynomials hain. Is se sabaq yeh mila ke root ya fraction aane se function transcendental nahin ban jata.
Kitab ki definition bohat chhoti hai: jo function algebraic nahin hai, woh transcendental function kehlata hai. Yani pehle check karo ke kya woh algebraic hai; agar nahin, to woh transcendental hai.
Kitab ki misalein: \(y = e^{x}\), \(y = 2^{x}\), \(y = \ln x\), \(y = \sin x\), \(y = \sin^{-1} x\), \(y = \sin x + \ln x\), \(y = e^{x^{2}}\), yeh sab transcendental functions hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
In sab misalon ko ghaur se dekhiye: har ek mein \(x\) kisi exponent (power) ke andar, kisi logarithm ke andar, ya kisi trigonometric ya inverse trigonometric function ke andar baitha hai. Jama, tafreeq, zarb, taqseem aur roots ki koi bhi mehdood zanjeer inhein nahin bana sakti, aur yeh kisi polynomial equation ko satisfy nahin karte. (Yeh poori tarah saabit karna ke maslan \(e^{x}\) algebraic nahin hai, is level se aage ki baat hai; hum ise maan lete hain.)
Ek aasan pehchaan: \(x^{2}\) mein variable base hai, is liye yeh algebraic hai. Lekin \(2^{x}\) mein variable exponent mein chala gaya, is liye yeh transcendental hai. Dono mein wahi 2 aur wahi \(x\) hain, sirf jagah badli hai, aur poori family badal gayi!

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh farq sirf naam ka nahin, graph ka bhi hai. Polynomial ka graph aakhir kaar \(x^{n}\) ki tarah behave karta hai, lekin \(2^{x}\) jaisa exponential function har polynomial se tez barhta hai, \(\ln x\) har power se aahista barhta hai, aur \(\sin x\) baar baar oopar neeche jhoolta rehta hai. Koi polynomial hamesha ke liye is tarah jhool nahin sakta. Isi liye transcendental functions ke graphs ko samajhne ke liye humein naye auzaar (properties) chahiye, jo hum 1.4 se seekhna shuru karenge.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
In mein se kaun algebraic hai aur kaun transcendental? \(\sqrt[3]{x^{2} + 7}\), \(3^{x} + x\), \(\frac{1}{x^{4} + 1}\), \(\cos x\).
Jawab: \(\sqrt[3]{x^{2}+7}\) aur \(\frac{1}{x^{4}+1}\) algebraic hain (sirf root aur taqseem); \(3^{x} + x\) aur \(\cos x\) transcendental hain (variable exponent mein, aur trigonometric function).

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Exam mein classify karna ho to yeh qadam uthaiye: function mein dhoondiye ke kya \(x\) kisi exponent mein, kisi \(\log\)/\(\ln\) mein, ya kisi trigonometric ya inverse trigonometric function mein hai. Agar hai (aur kat kar khatam nahin hota), to function transcendental hai; warna algebraic. Algebraic jawab ke saath uski polynomial equation likh dein (jaise upar wali misaal mein), to examiner ko poora yaqeen ho jata hai aur poore marks milte hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Algebraic function: \(x\) se mehdood \(+, -, \times, \div\) aur \(n^{\text{th}}\) roots se banta hai, aur \(y\) ki ek polynomial equation satisfy karta hai.
2. Transcendental function: har woh function jo algebraic nahin, jaise \(e^{x}\), \(2^{x}\), \(\ln x\), \(\sin x\), \(\sin^{-1} x\).
3. Roots aur fractions function ko algebraic hi rehne dete hain: \(\sqrt{x+1}\), \((x+1)^{3/2}\), \(\frac{x^{2}+1}{x-3}\).
4. Transcendental functions ka jor (jaise \(\sin x + \ln x\)) ya composition (jaise \(e^{x^{2}}\)) bhi transcendental hi hota hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\sqrt{x+1}\) ya \((x+1)^{3/2}\) ko root ya fractional power ki wajah se transcendental keh dena. Ghalat! Root lena algebraic operation hai.
2. \(2^{x}\) ko yeh soch kar algebraic kehna ke "2 to bas ek number hai". Asal baat yeh hai ke variable exponent mein hai, is liye yeh transcendental hai. \(x^{2}\) aur \(2^{x}\) ko kabhi ek na samjhein.
3. \(g(x) = \frac{x^{2}+1}{x-3}\) ke saath shart \(x \ne 3\) bhool jana. Rational function wahan defined nahin hota jahan denominator zero ho jaye.
